messages:
marcus: Heads up — during the staging base-image rollout I noticed repeated KMS decrypt failures and an RBAC change on the runtime service account around the same time. Putting this here so we can triage quickly. :eyes:

tanya: ack. logs? do we have the exact time window?

marcus: logs attached to the pipeline run but tl;dr: 2026-03-18T14:12Z -> a bunch of `DECRYPT_FAILURE` entries from gcloud kms and then several `Forbidden` from kube-apiserver for pods mounting /run/secrets.

sahil: hmm, that sounds like the KMS key rotation job kicked but the new key policy didn't include the runtime-SA. Could also be the image signing key change. Which key id?

marcus: key id is projects/redwood-keys/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/base-enc-v2. pipeline shows rotate-job v2 at 14:11:23.

ivy: we also got an alert on staging that container runtime pulled an unverified image (cosign verification failed) — alert id ALERT-2026-1387. Could be related: image sig verification failing -> fallback to pulling older tag that expects older key?

sec-bot: automated note: recent RBAC change PR #4532 merged by @tanya modified ClusterRoleBinding `runtime-exec` to include `system:serviceaccount:infra:runtime-sa`. Change timestamp 2026-03-18T14:09Z.

tanya: that PR was meant to add a missing permission for secret access. I didn't expect it to touch KMS key bindings. The binding only updated clusterrole subjects.

marcus: right. but timeline: RBAC change at 14:09, KMS rotate at 14:11, decrypt failures at 14:12. maybe the SA lost some access during the rollout window?

sahil: quick check: run this in staging: `kubectl auth can-i get secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:infra:runtime-sa -n infra`

tanya: ran it: `no` at 14:20. That explains Forbidden. But why was it `yes` pre-change? I'll diff the rolebinding.

ivy: we should also verify audit log entries in cloud audit logs for `Decrypt` RPCs to see which principal attempted access and which key version was used.

marcus: I pulled a snippet from cloud audit: `principalEmail: service-account@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `resourceName: keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/base-enc-v2/cryptoKeyVersions/3` and `status: PERMISSION_DENIED`.

tanya: ack. i'll revert the clusterrolebinding change temporarily to restore secret access, and we can reapply a minimal policy after confirming KMS IAM grant.

sahil: don't revert blindly if that change fixed something else. Suggest: 1) grant the runtime-SA `cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the new key version 3, 2) patch rolebinding subjects to include correct SA if missing.

ivy: also run a canary deploy for 10% of staging to validate cosign signature path. If verification still fails, we need to ensure cosign keys are in KMS and the pipeline has correct `KMS_KEY` env.

marcus: note: incident suspicion — a failed image verification fallback caused runtime to pull older images that assume older secret layout; that caused FK decrypt calls with the wrong key version, which failed because key access was removed for the service account. Cascading failure.

oncall: logging: please capture these three things and put into the incident ticket: 1) KMS decrypt RPC audit lines, 2) kube apiserver audit lines for `create pod`/`mount secret`, 3) pipeline env for cosign key. I'll create INC-2026-045 and assign to marcus.

tanya: extracting rolebinding diff now. small snippet: ```yaml
- subjects:
- - kind: ServiceAccount
-   name: runtime-sa
-   namespace: infra
+ subjects:
+ - kind: ServiceAccount
+   name: runtime-operator
+   namespace: infra
```

marcus: ah that explains it — the binding was changed to `runtime-operator` instead of `runtime-sa`. likely an edit mistake during PR. So runtime-sa lost clusterrole.

sahil: ok plan: (A) re-add `runtime-sa` to the clusterrolebinding with a safe patch, (B) grant KMS decrypt role to the runtime service account on key version 3, (C) re-run cosign verification canary, (D) audit for any images pulled unverified. Who owns A/B?

tanya: I'll own A (patch RBAC) and coordinate with infra-iam for B. Estimated ETA 30m.

ivy: I'll own C (canary) and D (audit), ETA 45m.

marcus: i'll open PR to add a check in the image rollout pipeline to validate KMS grant presence and run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` as a preflight. Also add cosign verification step earlier.

oncall: adding runbook note: during any base-image or KMS key rotation, pause the rollout if any RBAC or IAM changes are merged within the last 15 minutes. We'll add as a temporary guard.

sec-bot: recommended tickets: create a postmortem if incident escalates; include timeline, root cause (incorrect subject in ClusterRoleBinding + KMS rotate), mitigation, and a policy to require IAM gating for key rotates.

marcus: quick commands I'll run and paste results: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy base-enc-v2 --keyring=infra --location=global` and `kubectl get clusterrolebinding runtime-exec -o yaml`

tanya: hotfix applied: patched clusterrolebinding to include both `runtime-sa` and `runtime-operator`. kube `can-i` now returns `yes`.

ivy: cosign verification canary started — first batch passing. No new `DECRYPT_FAILURE` in the last 5m.

marcus: good. i'll leave INC-2026-045 with notes and add an action item: enforce PR checklist that any RBAC edit must be cross-checked with pending KMS rotations.

sahil: follow-up items: add automated test that validates `can-i` for critical SAs after RBAC merges, and run KMS IAM preflight in rotation job.

tanya: will open RBAC revert PR rollback-proof and add the checklist entry.

marcus: thanks all. will update ticket and start a short post-incident doc. :lock:
